hens_rule_text: Chickens are classed as farm animals and are banned within city limits, except in areas zoned agricultural.
permit_notes: No permit path exists for ordinary residential lots; chickens are simply prohibited outside agricultural zoning.
zoning_notes: Ordinance Sec. 92.05(3) bans keeping or running at large chickens and other farm animals within city limits except in agricultural districts. Unincorporated St. Lucie County, a separate jurisdiction, runs its own Backyard Chicken Program allowing up to 5 hens; that program does not apply inside Port St. Lucie city limits.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: City of Port St. Lucie (official X/Twitter account), backyard chickens not allowed statement citing Code of Ordinances

research_notes: The city's own official account and its 311 knowledge base both state plainly that backyard chickens are not allowed inside city limits, citing Ordinance Sec. 92.05(3); this is distinct from St. Lucie County's own Backyard Chicken Program for unincorporated county land, which several secondary sites conflate with the city.
